item.title: Russia increasingly reckless, says Nato’s Rutte as Germany blames Moscow for Leipzig drone incident – Europe live
item.description:
Germany blamed Russia for an attempted drone attack on a Leipzig airport last month, in a significant escalation of tensions between Europe and its eastern neighbor. Three explosive-laden drones were found around the airport, one near a Ukrainian plane transporting munitions. Berlin’s interior minister said Moscow was treating Europe with “open hostility” and announced countermeasures . EU leaders supported the move, and announced an initiative to boost defense cooperation with Ukraine and the UK. It is the first time Berlin has openly accused Russia of an attempted attack within German borders, Die Zeit’s foreign affairs editor said, describing it as a smart and “half-courageous” move that liberates the security forces, but also commits Germany to more direct clashes with Russia. — Tom Chivers

item.title: Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong could face life in prison after guilty plea
item.description:
Wong, 29, is accused of urging foreign powers to impose sanctions, blockades and other hostile measures against China Joshua Wong , one of Hong Kong’s most prominent pro-democracy activists, pleaded guilty on Wednesday to conspiring to seek foreign sanctions against Hong Kong and China, a national security charge that carries a maximum life sentence. Prosecutors have accused Wong, 29, of working with the exiled Hong Kong activist Nathan Law to urge foreign powers to impose sanctions, blockades or other hostile measures against China. item.description:

item.description:

item.title: ‘It always comes around’: fans react to conviction in Tupac Shakur’s murder 30 years later
item.description:
Jimmie “Chris” Duncan lived in a motel in Alexandria, Louisiana, for weeks until he found an apartment. Kathleen Flynn for ProPublica Jimmie “Chris” Duncan wiped the sweat off his forehead as he assessed his temporary home from the parking lot of a rundown motel in central Louisiana. Sure, there’s drug dealing and prostitution, he said on a recent summer afternoon. And he suspected his neighbors were cooking meth on a floor below the room he paid $350 a week to rent. But, he said, “I feel safe here. I mean, I’ve been on death row. I feel safe anywhere.” Duncan had spent the last three decades trying to prove his innocence after a jury convicted him of killing his former girlfriend’s toddler. item.title: Nepal search operations continue a week after catastrophic floods
item.description:
Authorities in Nepal continued mass burials after catastrophic floods roared down high mountain valleys in a vast torrent of destruction. The death toll is now over 1,000 people, with thousands still missing. Across the border in China, which has been less transparent, officials report just 16 deaths, but nearly 550 missing. Neil Connery of ITV News reports from the disaster zone.

item.title: Why a bill to juice condo construction died even though California lawmakers voted for it
item.description:
In summary Supporters said a condo construction bill was a key to unlocking the type of naturally affordable for-sale housing that California desperately needs. But deadlines matter. A bill that supporters hoped would kickstart California’s moribund condo industry and boost the scarce number of entry-level homeownership opportunities, died under mysterious circumstances at the stroke of midnight on Tuesday after failing to get a final vote before the end of the legislative session. Assembly Bill 1903 by Oakland Democratic lawmaker Buffy Wicks would have changed the way that disputes between homeowners and builders over purportedly shoddy construction are resolved in a way the bill’s author hoped would result in fewer defect lawsuits and less developer skittishness around building condos. . item.title: Decades after Tupac Shakur's murder, Duane 'Keffe D' Davis convicted
item.description:
After three decades, there is a conviction in one of the country's most infamous unsolved killings. A Nevada jury found Duane "Keffe D" Davis guilty of orchestrating the 1996 murder of hip-hop superstar Tupac Shakur. Prosecutors argued he ordered the killing and sought revenge after Shakur and members of his entourage attacked Davis's nephew. Amna Nawaz discussed more with Joel Anderson.

item.title: Once again, Trump wants the FCC to put a bandage on his thin skin | Tom Wheeler
item.description:
The president is lashing out at an NBC host. As the agency’s former chair, I can only hope it stands up for free speech Will the FCC chairperson again abuse his authority over broadcast licenses to put a Band-Aid on Donald Trump’s thin skin? Since the opening days of the Trump presidency, Brendan Carr has acted as the president’s attack dog to coerce broadcasters to say things that please his client. item.title: Guinea-Bissau referendum tests democratic future
item.description:
Referendum result means fewer seats in parliament and new rules on candidates, ahead of December elections Guinea-Bissau voters have approved a new constitution, which critics say will undermine democracy, that significantly expands presidential powers ahead of elections due in December. According to provisional results, 70% of voters approved sweeping changes in the tiny west African state’s first constitutional amendment since revisions that ended the one-party socialist state more than three decades ago. item.title: 'Dangerous consequences': Iran warns US after alleged strike on wedding
item.description:
US Central Command has released footage that purportedly shows missile and drone strikes being fired at Iranian military targets. Footage of some of the aftermath of the US attacks was shared on social media, showing shrapnel damage on a home in Sirik, southern Iran, where a wedding celebration was taking place. Five people were killed and 68 were wounded. Iran retaliated shortly afterwards, with video shared by Iranian media said to show missiles being fired towards Jordan.
